author: EmuCore - Hub
title: DuckStation moves overscan cleanup into per-game display data
summary: Measured GameDB crop offsets remove unused PlayStation border pixels title by title, avoiding a global crop that would cut real artwork from games with different active display areas.
heroAlt: Visual evidence from DuckStation pull request #3646: GameDB: Adjust cropping in a number of titles (part 1)

sourceLabels.duckstation-pr-3646: GameDB: Adjust cropping in a number of titles (part 1)

blocks.text: The PlayStation framebuffer is larger than every game's intended picture

Many games leave stable blank or noisy columns around the active image, but the amount is not universal. A global crop that looks correct for one title can remove interface art or reveal a border in another. Pull request #3646 records crop behavior in GameDB, where it can follow a serial and region instead of turning a collection of title-specific observations into one risky renderer default.
Offsets describe presentation, not a rewritten framebuffer

The change adjusts how DuckStation presents the active display area; it does not modify the pixels generated by the emulated GPU. Examples include an eight-pixel correction for Arc the Lad III, Breath of Fire IV, Dino Crisis, Echo Night, and Galerians, while Dragon Warrior VII uses a larger value. That variation is the point: each entry documents its own border rather than inheriting a convenient number from another game.
Before-and-after pairs reveal borders and over-cropping separately

The source supplies matched captures for several games, letting reviewers distinguish removal of unused edge pixels from accidental zoom. Chrono Cross was explicitly struck from the set after its result exposed borders differently, a useful sign that entries were not accepted merely because a smaller image looked cleaner. The review standard should preserve HUD elements, subtitles, and scene edges while hiding only pixels the title never treats as active content.
Serial coverage and unusual video modes need regression checks

Validation should open each affected serial in menus, gameplay, FMV, and any 240p or interlaced mode it uses. Compare the reported GameDB crop with crop disabled and verify that aspect ratio remains stable. Regional variants should not inherit an offset unless their active area was checked. A follow-up audit can also detect entries that switch display width mid-game, where one static offset may need a narrower scope.
Cropping is safest as compatibility data: measured per title, reversible, and separate from the emulated framebuffer.
